title: Lloyds climbs global rankings for AI talent and leadership
short: Lloyds Banking Group has maintained its 15th position globally in the October 2026 Evident AI Index, retaining its ranking for a second consecutive year and remaining the highest placed bank in the UK.
quick: Lloyds Banking Group has maintained its 15th position globally in the October 2026 Evident AI Index, retaining its ranking for a second consecutive year and remaining the highest placed bank in the UK.
lead: Lloyds Banking Group has maintained its 15th position globally in the October 2026 Evident AI Index, retaining its ranking for a second consecutive year and remaining the highest placed bank in the UK.
blocks: Lloyds Banking Group has maintained its 15th position globally in the October 2026 Evident AI Index, retaining its ranking for a second consecutive year and remaining the highest placed bank in the UK. The Group's overall score increased from 45.0 to 55.2, marking a 10.2-point improvement year on year. Across the 50 institutions assessed in the index across North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific, the average score increased by 26%, or 9.6 points, moving from 36.5 to 46.1. The benchmark evaluates institutions using 75 indicators across four pillars.

Lloyds ranks in the global top 10 in three of the index's four pillars and joint first globally for talent development and Responsible AI leadership. In the Talent pillar, which accounts for 45% of the total index weighting, the Group rose six places year-on-year to rank 10th globally. This improvement follows continued investment in specialist talent and workforce-wide skills. Earlier this year, Lloyds announced plans for more than 1,000 agentic AI roles to support its AI build-out during the year, alongside AI engineering apprenticeships. The Group also gained seven places in the Leadership pillar to reach sixth globally, and maintained sixth position globally for Transparency in responsible artificial intelligence deployment.

Lloyds expects next-generation AI to deliver more than £100 million in additional value during 2026. This is supported by the continued scaling of Envoy, described by Lloyds as its secure and governed platform for building, sharing and running AI agents across the organisation. Commenting on the results, Rohit Dhawan, Director of AI and Advanced Analytics at Lloyds, stated that the group's progress reflects investment in people, skills and responsible deployment, providing an external measure of progress as AI is applied to support colleagues and deliver practical value for customers.

title: Lloyds Banking Group merges transport brands under new Lloyds Auto name
short: Black Horse, Lex Autolease and Tusker are to unite under a single customer-facing brand, according to an announcement by Lloyds Banking Group.
quick: Black Horse, Lex Autolease and Tusker are to unite under a single customer-facing brand, according to an announcement by Lloyds Banking Group.
lead: Black Horse, Lex Autolease and Tusker are to unite under a single customer-facing brand, according to an announcement by Lloyds Banking Group.
blocks: Lloyds Banking Group has announced that Black Horse, Lex Autolease and Tusker will come together under a single customer-facing brand named Lloyds Auto. The change aims to create a simpler and more consistent experience across the Group's Transport business for motor finance, leasing and salary sacrifice customers and partners. Preston Rogers, Interim Managing Director for Transport at Lloyds Banking Group, says the move builds on the heritage and expertise of the three existing names to set the business up for the future, reflecting growing expectations for efficient and joined-up services.
No immediate changes for existing customers

Lloyds Banking Group states that there are no immediate changes for customers or partners, and existing products, agreements, terms and services will continue to work as they do today. Clients will continue to be supported through existing channels while the Lloyds Auto brand is introduced gradually over time. Customers and partners will be contacted directly when they need to know about any changes.

The consolidation allows Lloyds Banking Group to focus its investment on the propositions, platforms and support considered most important for the future. Alongside the announcement, the Group issued a security warning, noting that it will never ask customers to move money, transfer funds or share security details as part of the brand change, and that any contact requesting such action is a scam.
